abstracts.title: Individualized sequencing of targeted immunotherapies in generalized myasthenia gravis across distinct patient profiles.
abstracts.abstract: Background Targeted immunotherapies have expanded treatment options for acetylcholine receptor antibody-positive generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG), but evidence regarding their sequencing and individualized therapeutic pathways remains limited. Methods We describe seven selected adults with AChR-positive gMG managed through individualized targeted-treatment pathways involving administered and, in some cases, planned sequential therapy. Treatment selection was guided by disease severity, corticosteroid-related risks, presence of thymoma, comorbidities, peripheral venous access and the need for rapid clinical improvement and/or sustained disease management. Results Across the seven cases, FcRn antagonists were used for rapid symptom control, corticosteroid dose reduction and bridging therapy while the appropriate vaccinations required before planned complement inhibition or B-cell depletion therapy were completed. Rituximab was selected as a long-term B-cell-directed immunosuppressive strategy, particularly in recent-onset gMG. Ravulizumab was planned as a long-term, non-steroidal immunosuppressive therapy in thymoma-associated myasthenia gravis and in chronic gMG with symptoms re…

abstracts.title: Current and Emerging Therapies for Generalized Myasthenia Gravis: Toward Precision Medicine.
abstracts.abstract: The therapeutic landscape of myasthenia gravis (MG) has changed substantially with advances in immunopathogenesis and the introduction of targeted, mechanism-based immunotherapies. For decades, treatment relied primarily on corticosteroids and conventional immunosuppressive agents, which are effective but often limited by delayed onset, long-term toxicity, and incomplete disease control. This review summarizes current and emerging therapies for generalized MG, focusing on mechanisms of action, clinical efficacy, safety, and practical considerations, while also addressing real-world evidence, treatment switching and sequencing, and factors relevant to individualized decision-making. Complement-targeted therapies, including eculizumab, ravulizumab, zilucoplan, gefurulimab, and the emerging RNA interference-based agent cemdisiran, and neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) inhibitors, including efgartigimod, rozanolixizumab, and nipocalimab, have substantially expanded therapeutic options. B cell-targeted therapies, particularly rituximab and inebilizumab, have also broadened the therapeutic landscape, especially for refractory disease and muscle-specific kinase antibody-positive MG. Emerging a…

abstracts.title: The effect of FcRn inhibition on overlapping autoimmune comorbidity in AChR-seropositive generalized myasthenia gravis.
abstracts.abstract: Introduction Generalized Myasthenia gravis (gMG) is a rare autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction caused by IgG autoantibodies against antigens in the postsynaptic cleft. This study aimed to assess the real-world effectiveness and safety of Efgartigimod (EFG) in AChR-positive gMG with overlapping autoimmune comorbidity. Methods EFG was administered as 4 consecutive weekly infusions or injections. Myasthenia Gravis Activity of Daily Living (MG-ADL) and Myasthenia Gravis quantitative (QMG) scales were administered at baseline and after 4 weeks. Clinical data on autoimmune comorbidities and prednisone use were collected. Results 35 patients (20 women, mean age 53.6 years) received EFG, with a significant and clinical improvement in both MG-ADL and QMG scores. MG-ADL responder rate (MG-ADL reduction≥2) was 79%, while 68% on QMG (QMG reduction≥3); Minimal symptoms expression was reached in 4 patients, with a mean reduction in daily prednisone dose of 8 mg. Overlapping autoimmune comorbidity was reported in 12 gMG patients (34%). gMG patients with Stiff-Person syndrome, type 1 Diabetes and Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome benefited more from EFG with a higher reduction on MG…

Regimen-stratified Bayesian model-based meta-analysis of targeted biologics in generalised myasthenia gravis: efficacy comparison, mechanism-level class contrast, and endpoint sensitivity with model-…
abstracts.abstract: Nine targeted biologics spanning four mechanisms have reached phase III development for generalised myasthenia gravis, yet no cross-programme comparison accounts for the distinct continuous versus cyclical dosing patterns or integrates both patient-reported (MG-ADL) and clinician-assessed (QMG) scales. We performed a regimen-stratified Bayesian model-based meta-analysis (MBMA) to compare efficacy, evaluate mechanism-level class differences, and inform trial design. Longitudinal MG-ADL and QMG data were extracted from nine placebo-controlled phase III trials. Six hierarchical nonlinear Emax models were fitted with inverse-variance weighting. Drug-specific maximum efficacy, net benefit over placebo, week 26 predictions, time to the minimum clinically important difference (MCID), cumulative efficacy, ranking probabilities, and mechanism-level class contrasts were derived. Robustness was assessed via model comparison, prior sensitivity, and Leave-one-study-out analyses on both scales. Endpoint-sensitivity simulation and a treatment-selection framework were appended. The study was registered with PROSPERO: CRD420261288549. On MG-ADL, zilucoplan led with the highest Emax (4.8 points; 95…

abstracts.title: Age and Treatment Efficacy in Myasthenia Gravis: A Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis, and Meta-Regression.
abstracts.abstract: Background Myasthenia gravis (MG) is increasingly concentrated in older adults, and age may shift the balance of benefit and risk for MG therapies. This study seeks to evaluate the effect of age on treatment efficacy in clinical trials of MG. Methods PubMed and Cochrane Library were searched and clinical trials enrolling adults with MG that reported the quantitative myasthenia gravis (QMG) score and the myasthenia gravis activities of daily living (MG-ADL) scale were included. Of 2214 records identified, 18 trials met inclusion criteria. Random-effects meta-analysis was used to pool treatment effects, and random-effects meta-regression evaluated trial-level mean baseline age as a modifier of treatment efficacy. Results Eighteen trials published from 2017 to 2025 included 1823 participants (982 assigned to treatment and 841 to control). Pooled effects favored treatment over control for the QMG (MD -2.402; 95% CI, -3.099 to -1.706; I2 = 60.7%) and MG-ADL scores (MD, -1.591; 95% CI, -1.874 to -1.309; I2 = 0.0%). In meta-regression, higher mean trial age was associated with attenuation of treatment benefit on the QMG scale (β per 10 years, 1.21; 95% CI, 0.02 to 2.42; p = 0.047). This…

abstracts.title: Real-world Treatment Patterns Among Patients with Generalized Myasthenia Gravis in the United States.
abstracts.abstract: Introduction Conventional treatments for generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) include acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (AChEi), systemic corticosteroids, and non-steroidal immunosuppressants; standard of care for exacerbation or myasthenic crisis includes immunoglobulin and plasmapheresis; newer advanced treatments include B-cell depleting agents, complement-5 inhibitors (C5i), and neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) blockers. This study described real-world treatment patterns with currently available therapies and prevalence of myasthenia gravis (MG)-related clinical events (exacerbations or crises) among patients with gMG in the US. Methods Adults with gMG were identified from Komodo Research Data (January 1, 2017-February 28, 2025). Index date was the first MG diagnosis by a neurologist. Patients were followed for ≥ 12 months post-index. Treatment sequencing was characterized by individual classes and broader treatment types (conventional treatments, advanced immunotherapies, immunoglobulin). A treatment episode was defined based on treatment changes (discontinuation, switch, augmentation/add-on, or drop), with any remaining or newly initiated/added treatment marking a new episode. abstracts.title: Targeted Therapies in Generalized Myasthenia Gravis: An Umbrella Review of Evidence Quality and Overlap.
abstracts.abstract: Generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) is an antibody-mediated autoimmune disorder in which complement C5 inhibitors and neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) antagonists have expanded therapeutic options, while rituximab remains used off-label in selected patients. We conducted an umbrella review to critically appraise systematic reviews and evidence syntheses evaluating complement inhibitors and/or FcRn antagonists within a therapeutic framework that also included rituximab. MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Epistemonikos, Google Scholar, and supplementary citation sources were searched from 2015 onward, with an updated search on 15 August 2026. Methodological quality was assessed with AMSTAR 2 and primary-study overlap with the corrected covered area (CCA) and GROOVE. Ten reviews/evidence syntheses met eligibility criteria. Complement inhibitors and FcRn antagonists were generally associated with improvements in MG-ADL and QMG, although estimates and rankings varied. AMSTAR 2 rated one review as high confidence, four as low confidence, and five as critically low confidence. Primary-study overlap was very high (CCA 32.59%), with 36 of 45 pairwise comparisons classified as very high. Comparative eviden…

data.warnings_and_cautions: 5 WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS Infections: Delay administration of VYVGART HYTRULO to patients with an active infection. Monitor for signs and symptoms of infection in patients treated with VYVGART HYTRULO. If serious infection occurs, administer appropriate treatment and consider withholding VYVGART HYTRULO until the infection has resolved. ( 5.1 ) Hypersensitivity Reactions: Anaphylaxis, hypotension leading to syncope, angioedema, dyspnea, rash, and urticaria have occurred in patients treated with VYVGART HYTRULO or intravenous efgartigimod alfa-fcab product. If a hypersensitivity reaction occurs, the healthcare professional should institute appropriate measures if needed or the patient should seek medical attention. ( 4 , 5.2 ) Infusion/injection-Related Reactions: If a severe infusion/injection-related reaction occurs, initiate appropriate therapy; consider the risks and benefits of readministering. sections.text: Thirty-seven trials test FcRn inhibitors in myasthenia gravis (MG), with 24 in Phase 3 and 8 in Phase 2.
The main sponsors are argenx (11 trials), UCB (10 trials), J&J (5 trials), and Immunovant (3 trials).
Approved FcRn inhibitors for MG include efgartigimod alfa, nipocalimab, and rozanolixizumab.
One Phase 3 trial of batoclimab was terminated due to a sponsor decision.
A Phase 2 trial of ALXN1830 was withdrawn due to a sponsor decision to terminate the program.
The site's risk model estimates a typical trial attrition risk of 13.6% and a median risk of 24.9% for FcRn inhibitors in MG.
A 2026 case series describes FcRn antagonists used for rapid symptom control and corticosteroid reduction in AChR-positive gMG.
A 2026 real-world study of 35 AChR-positive gMG patients showed a 79% response rate on MG-ADL and a mean 8 mg/day prednisone dose reduction with efgartigimod.
A 2026 umbrella review found that FcRn antagonists are generally associated with improvements in MG-ADL and QMG scores, though evidence quality varies.
FcRn inhibitors compete with complement inhibitors (e.g., eculizumab) and B-cell therapies (e.g., rituximab) in gMG.
A direct comparative Phase 3 trial (NCT07217587) is ongoing to evaluate nipocalimab versus efgartigimod in generalized MG.

read: Mechanism evidence: Strong real-world and clinical trial data support FcRn inhibition for symptom control and steroid-sparing in gMG.
Competitive position: FcRn inhibitors are established in the market with multiple approved agents and ongoing comparative trials.
Open questions: Long-term safety, comparative efficacy versus other biologics, and optimal sequencing remain active areas of study.
would_change: New head-to-head trial data showing inferiority to competing mechanisms (e.g., complement inhibitors) would change this judgement.
Emergence of significant long-term safety signals in post-marketing studies could shift the risk-benefit assessment.
